tiebreak_notes: AFC No. 1 seed (DEN vs NE, both 14-3, no head-to-head game, conference records both 9-3): 'Denver finished ahead of New England based on common games (Denver 6-0 to New England 5-1 against: Cincinnati, Las Vegas, NY Giants, NY Jets and Tennessee).' [Corroborated by NBC Sports Boston and 98.5 The Sports Hub, which say NE's Week 1 loss to LV was the difference.]
AFC No. 5 seed (HOU vs BUF, both 12-5): 'Houston finished ahead of Buffalo based on head-to-head victory.'
NFC No. 2 seed (CHI vs PHI, both 11-6): 'Chicago finished ahead of Philadelphia based on head-to-head victory.'
NFC South, three-way tie at 8-9 (CAR, TB, ATL): 'Carolina finished ahead of Tampa Bay and Atlanta based on head-to-head record (Carolina 3-1 to Tampa Bay 2-2 and Atlanta 1-3).'

NFC No. 5 seed (LAR vs SF, both 12-5, same division, so the division tiebreak applies: head-to-head split 1-1, division records both 4-2): 'LA Rams finished ahead of San Francisco based on common games (LA Rams 9-3 to San Francisco 8-4 against: Arizona, Atlanta, Carolina, Houston, Indianapolis, Jacksonville, New Orleans, Seattle, Tampa Bay and Tennessee).' [The common-games step is from Wikipedia only; I found no independent text confirming it. The seed order itself matches NFL.com.]
NFC No. 7: GB (9-7-1, .559) beat MIN (9-8, .529) on winning percentage; the tie game decided it, not a tiebreaker.
